transcript.text: Just had a new induction hob fitted, Beko. When I put my saucepan on it just flashes a U and doesn't heat. Is it faulty? It's brand new!!

A flashing 'U' on an induction hob usually means it cannot detect a suitable pan, rather than indicating a fault with the appliance itself. Induction hobs only heat magnetic cookware (like cast iron or certain stainless steels) that is flat and large enough to cover the zone. Please try these two quick checks:
1. Take a fridge magnet and stick it to the base of your saucepan. If it does not stick firmly, the pan will not work on this hob.
2. Ensure the pan base is completely flat (not domed) and covers at least 12cm of the heating zone. If you have another magnetic pan that works elsewhere, try that one. If the 'U' still flashes with a known good pan, there may be an installation or control issue.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

I tried a magnet: it doesn't stick to my saucepans, but it does stick to my cast-iron casserole, and the casserole heated up fine. The pan is centred and covers most of the zone too. So is it just my pans then?!

Yes, it is just your pans. Your saucepans simply do not have the right material to interact with the hob's magnetic field. You will need to use compatible pans for that zone.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]

candidates: Hob control fault or installation issue (low)
plan: They asked: "Is it faulty?" - answer that first.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Beko; code U.
The fault they reported is: "flashes U and doesn't heat". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the one or two safe checks, or the one question, that would best tell those causes apart. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

Explain what the error code means using ERROR CODES. If ERROR CODES does not resolve it, say plainly that you cannot confirm what it means on their model (it may not be an error code at all, for example part of the model name), never guess a meaning, and work from the symptoms.

claimsRejected.claim: the hob cannot detect a suitable pan because they are not magnetic
As you found with the magnet test and the cast-iron casserole, induction hobs only work with ferrous metal cookware (like iron or magnetic stainless steel).

plan: They asked: "So is it just my pans then?!" - answer that first.
Already told them (do not repeat any of it; build on it): turn 1: gives check.

Checks they have done and what they found: tested pan compatibility with magnet - magnet does not stick to saucepans but sticks to cast-iron casserole; tested heating with known good pan - casserole heated up fine.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Beko; code U.
The fault they reported is: "flashes U and doesn't heat". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 2: the checks they reported did not fix it. Say what that suggests, then ask for the model number so we can find the right part; say it is usually on the underside of the hob or on the guarantee card. If the label cannot be reached right now (for example the door will not open), say it can wait.
